summary.text: A linear map is a function between vector spaces that respects vector addition and scalar multiplication.
It does not matter whether you apply the map before or after adding and scaling, so it preserves linear combinations.
A matrix is the standard example, and rotations and reflections are simple cases.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: A linear map always sends the origin to the origin

facts.label: Matrices
facts.value: Maps between finite-dimensional spaces can be written as matrices

facts.label: Same space
facts.value: Called a linear transformation or linear endomorphism

facts.label: Not linear
facts.value: Adding one to every real number

items.prompt: The function that adds one to every real number fails to be linear. What goes wrong?

options.label: It moves zero to a different point
It cannot be drawn as a graph

items.explain: A linear map always sends the origin to the origin, and adding one sends zero to one.

items.prompt: T is a linear map. You add two vectors and then apply T. A friend applies T to each vector and then adds. How do the results compare?

options.label: They differ by a factor of two
They agree only for the zero vector

items.explain: It does not matter whether the map is applied before or after addition and scalar multiplication.

items.prompt: A linear map squashes space, and you feed it a flat sheet that passes through the origin. What can come out?

options.label: Any flat sheet or line anywhere
A sheet, a line, or the origin, all through the origin
Only a sheet that misses the origin
Only another sheet, never a line

items.explain: A plane through the origin maps to a plane through the origin, a line through the origin, or just the origin.

items.prompt: A real matrix with 3 rows and 2 columns multiplies column vectors. Which spaces does it connect?
items.explain: An m × n real matrix defines a linear map from ℝⁿ to ℝᵐ.

items.prompt: Which of these behaves as a linear function of a random variable?
items.explain: Expected value is linear, since E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y], but variance is not, since Var(aX) = a²Var(X).

items.prompt: A student differentiates a sum of two scaled functions by differentiating each one separately and then combining. Which property allows this?
items.explain: Differentiation is a linear map: d/dx(af(x) + bg(x)) = adf(x)/dx + bdg(x)/dx.
